text:
Mira Patel: Heads-up — Everleaf onboarding flagged a few items in their security questionnaire. They want: encryption at rest details + KMS/HSM usage, SOC2 status and a copy or timeline, and whether we can sign a DPA that lists subprocessors. Pasting the exact customer question below.

Mira Patel: ```
Q1: Do you encrypt data at rest? If so, what KMS/HSM do you use, who holds the keys, and can we have a key separation option?
Q2: Do you have a current SOC2 report? If not, expected completion date and evidence of controls in place.
Q3: Will you accept our DPA redlines around subprocessors and data residency?
```

Tom Ellis: Quick answers in-thread first pass — yes we encrypt at rest. We use customer-data keys in our KMS for private deployments; hosted customers are on AWS KMS with envelope encryption and CMKs controlled by Redwood. For Dedicated we can support customer-managed keys via KMS integration (bring-your-own-KMS). SOC2: in progress, Type II expected end of Q3; we can provide interim control evidence (policy docs, audit logs, control matrix). DPA: we generally accept limited redlines; anything adding mandatory flow-downs or indemnities needs legal.

Sasha Green: Suggested customer-facing wording for Q1 (short): "Yes — all customer data is encrypted at rest. For Hosted customers we use cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) with envelope encryption; for Dedicated and Private deployments we offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed options where required. Key rotation and access policies are enforced, and we can provide a KMS architecture diagram on request." Feel free to copy/edit. :+1:

Ken Wu: For the SOC2 ask, send the SOC2 readiness pack for now: control matrix + list of compensating controls + penetration test summary. Mention timeline and that SOC2 Type II report will be shared under NDA when complete. Also include a note about continuous monitoring (console traces + alerts).

Tom Ellis: For the DPA redlines: we can accept a subprocessors appendix, but we push back on language that requires prior written consent for every change — propose a 30-day notice + right to object process instead. Also we don't agree to unlimited liabilities; leave to Legal. Tagging @legal for formal review when Mira has their redlines.

Sasha Green: Concrete snippet for DPA response (short): "We can sign a standard DPA. We provide a subprocessors appendix and will give 30 days' notice before adding subprocessors. For Dedicated/Private customers, we support on-prem or VPC options to meet residency requirements."

Mira Patel: This is great — thanks. I'll draft a reply to Everleaf with Sasha's Q1 wording + Ken's SOC2 pack link and Tom's DPA snippet. Quick question: do we have the KMS architecture diagram ready to attach or should I request it from infra?

OnboardBot: Reminder queued — attach SOC2 readiness pack and KMS diagram before sending. Due in 72h if not completed.

Tom Ellis: KMS diagram exists in drive: /security/kms-arch/kms-overview-2025.pdf — Mira, I can attach. Also, if Everleaf requests HSM attestation, we can provide vendor certs for HSM-backed deployments.

Mira Patel: Perfect. I'll assemble and send today, copying Legal on the DPA redlines. Will post final thread message after I send. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
